history.hpi: Patient was gardening in her backyard when she developed progressive wheeze and chest tightness over the past 20 minutes. She has a known history of mild persistent asthma, typically well controlled, with symptoms usually triggered by seasonal outdoor allergens. She used her home albuterol inhaler once with only slight improvement before calling 911.
history.lastOralIntake: Water approximately 1 hour prior to symptom onset
history.events: Symptoms began while gardening outdoors; used home inhaler once with minimal relief, husband called 911 when wheeze persisted

scene.location: Single-family home, patient seated on back porch steps just outside a garden
scene.time: 3:15 PM, weekday, warm and dry afternoon
scene.bystanders: Husband present, called 911 when inhaler use did not resolve symptoms
visualCues: Patient seated upright, mild use of accessory muscles
Audible expiratory wheeze from across the room
Home albuterol MDI visible on porch table
Freshly turned garden soil and pollen-heavy flowering plants nearby

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 26-year-old female seated upright on the porch steps with audible expiratory wheeze, mild accessory muscle use, and able to speak in full sentences.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mild tachypnea, audible expiratory wheeze bilaterally, mild intercostal retractions
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and regular
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "My chest feels tight and I keep wheezing, my inhaler barely helped."

transitions.condition: Crew assesses breath sounds and work of breathing, applies supplemental oxygen, and administers a nebulized albuterol/ipratropium treatment for the bronchospasm.

phases.name: Duoneb and O2 started
phases.description: Crew applies supplemental oxygen and administers a combined albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer treatment for the mild bronchospasm.
phases.triggerCondition: After assessing breath sounds and work of breathing, the crew recognizes mild bronchospasm from a wheezing asthmatic and initiates oxygen along with a nebulized bronchodilator treatment.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Nebulizer mask in place, mild wheeze persisting, less accessory muscle use
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and regular
otherFindings: Nebulizer treatment in progress via mask
Oxygen applied via nasal cannula prior to nebulizer
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's already starting to help a little."

expectedActions.shortAction: Auscultate breath sounds, assess air entry and work of breathing
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Air entry (normal vs. diminished, prolonged expiratory phase). Breath sounds (wheezes, crackles, rales, rhonchi, diminished, clear)
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms bronchospasm as the cause of distress and establishes a baseline to track response to treatment.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula, titrate to SpO2 94-98%
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Give supplemental oxygen for dyspnea to a target of 94–98% saturation. Escalate from a nasal cannula as needed to reach this goal
expectedActions.rationale: Corrects mild hypoxia and supports oxygenation while bronchodilator therapy takes effect.

expectedActions.shortAction: Albuterol 5 mg nebulized with ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized, combined treatment
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: albuterol 5 mg nebulized (or 6 puffs metered dose inhaler) should be administered to all patients in respiratory distress with signs of bronchospasm (e.g., known asthmatics, quiet wheezers). Repeat at this dose with unlimited frequency for ongoing respiratory distress. Ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized should be given up to 3 doses in conjunction with albuterol
expectedActions.rationale: Combined bronchodilator therapy relieves bronchospasm and improves air movement in wheezing asthma exacerbations.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.condition: Wheeze and work of breathing improve after oxygen and the nebulized bronchodilator treatment; patient is packaged and transported with ongoing reassessment.
Crew delays or fails to administer the nebulized bronchodilator treatment despite ongoing bronchospasm, and the patient's work of breathing worsens.

phases.name: Improved after treatment
phases.description: Wheeze and accessory muscle use have resolved after oxygen and a single nebulizer treatment. Patient is comfortable, speaking easily, and ready for transport.
phases.triggerCondition: After completing the nebulized albuterol/ipratropium treatment with supplemental oxygen, the patient's bronchospasm resolves and she is prepared for transport.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Clear bilateral breath sounds, no accessory muscle use
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and regular
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I can breathe so much easier now, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess breath sounds, vital signs, and work of breathing after treatment
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Document key aspects of the exam at baseline and after each intervention: Respiratory rate, Oxygen saturation, Use of accessory muscles, Breath sounds and quality, Response to interventions
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms resolution of bronchospasm and guides the transport decision.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

phases.name: Duoneb delayed
phases.description: The crew delays administering the nebulized bronchodilator treatment. Wheeze and work of breathing worsen, and the patient becomes more anxious and tachypneic.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew focuses on other tasks and delays the nebulized albuterol/ipratropium treatment despite persistent bronchospasm, allowing distress to progress.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Increased wheeze, increased accessory muscle use, more labored
otherFindings: Patient more anxious, speaking in shorter phrases
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's getting... harder to breathe... please help."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize worsening bronchospasm; start albuterol 5 mg with ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized without further delay
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: albuterol 5 mg nebulized (or 6 puffs metered dose inhaler) should be administered to all patients in respiratory distress with signs of bronchospasm (e.g., known asthmatics, quiet wheezers). Repeat at this dose with unlimited frequency for ongoing respiratory distress
expectedActions.rationale: Delayed bronchodilator therapy allows progression of bronchospasm; prompt treatment is still indicated once recognized.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)
